title: 4GE1-style exam questions: River regimes and storm hydrographs (1.1)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y10 lesson 29 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 29: River regimes and storm hydrographs (1.1). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Explain how physical and human factors affect the shape of a storm hydrograph.' Write in the portal response box.
questions.a: Physical: slope, rock type, soil saturation, basin size and shape; human: urbanisation, deforestation, drainage; each linked to lag time and peak discharge
questions.model: Teacher plans it first: P1 rock type (impermeable: more runoff, short lag); P2 antecedent rainfall; P3 urbanisation; P4 deforestation; link each to peak and lag.

questions.q: Suggest why a river's regime might change after a dam is built.
questions.a: Water is stored and released steadily (1), so peaks are lower and low flows higher (1); abstraction may reduce total flow (1)

questions.q: Why are hydrographs useful for flood prediction?
questions.a: They show how fast and high a river rises after rain (1), so warnings can be timed (1)

questions.q: Peak rainfall is at 9 am; peak discharge at 7 pm. Calculate the lag time.
questions.model: 9 am to 7 pm. 9 am to 12 noon is 3 hours. 12 noon to 7 pm is 7 hours. 3 + 7 = 10 hours.

questions.q: From the chart, state the peak discharge.
Explain why deforestation shortens lag time.
questions.a: Less interception (1), so more rain reaches the ground and runs off quickly (1)

questions.q: Big question: why does one river flood within hours of a storm while another rises slowly?
questions.a: Steep, impermeable, urban or saturated basins send water quickly; gentle, permeable, forested basins slow it
